diagnosis: The scenario fails the Weak Arm gate because checks C1 and C2 are satisfied by generic 'pre-load inspection' commitments, which do not require the hidden information in PF1 or PF2. The model defaults to a standard inspection for all vehicles (V-1, V-2, V-3) rather than the specific 'V-2 rear-suspension inspection' required by PF2/C5 or the 'equipment-coordination commitment' required by PF1/C6.

C1.why: The temporary V-2 payload limit changes the 3,800-kilogram engineering pallet assignment from V-2 being a nominally valid option to exactly V-1 and requires a V-2 rear-suspension inspection commitment, not merely confirmation that the 3,000-kilogram limit is respected.

C2.why: The approved V-3 inverter compatibility changes the refrigerated crate assignment from an otherwise open vehicle choice to exactly V-3 and requires a V-3-specific equipment-coordination commitment confirming inverter compatibility and temperature-control unit functionality; a standard pre-load inspection alone is insufficient.
